<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company issued $25.0 million in principal aggregate amount of 7.5556% convertible subordinated notes due 2014 on February 4, 2009.&#160; In connection with the issuance of these notes, the Company was required to deposit approximately $9.4 million in escrow for up to twenty-four months for the purposes of paying the interest on the notes and the make-whole payments upon conversion or redemption.&#160; As the result of the conversion of $24.5 million of these notes in 2009, approximately $9.3 million was released from restricted cash to fund the make-whole interest payment.&#160; The remaining $0.5 million in principal aggregate amount was prepaid in 2011 and $0.1 million was released from restricted cash to fund the make-whole interest payment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;text-indent:1.1pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Property and Equipment</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;text-indent:1.1pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property and equipment consists of furniture, office and laboratory equipment, and leasehold improvements stated at cost. Furniture and office and laboratory equipment are depreciated on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives ranging from five to seven years. Leasehold improvements are amortized on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the lease term or the estimated useful life of the asset.&#160; Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Deferred Financing Costs</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred financing costs represent legal and other costs and fees incurred to negotiate and obtain debt financing. Deferred financing costs are capitalized and amortized using the effective interest method over the life of the applicable financing. Deferred financing costs were approximately $0.3 million and $0.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160; Amortization expense was $0.5 million, $0.2 million and $1.8 million in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160; Approximately $0.4 million of</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-12<a name="PB_12_015323_7056"></a></font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">deferred financings costs related to a financing that was not completed were expensed to general and administrative expense in 2011.&#160; The Company incurred approximately $1.6 million in deferred financing costs from the issuance of $25.0 million in principal aggregate amount of 7.5556% convertible subordinated notes due 2014 in 2009.&#160; Additionally, as a result of the conversion of $24.5 million of these notes, amortization of the deferred financing costs was accelerated and amortization expense of $1.6 million was recorded in 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Identifiable Intangible Asset</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Identifiable intangible asset consisted of the assembled workforce acquired in the merger with Maxim Pharmaceuticals Inc. (&#147;Maxim&#148;) in January&nbsp;2006. The assembled workforce was being amortized on the greater of the straight-line basis or actual assembled workforce turnover over six years. The gross carrying amount of the assembled workforce was $0.5 million, which was fully amortized in 2010 resulting in a remaining balance of zero at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010.&#160; Approximately $0.2 million of amortization was recorded in 2009 due to the layoff of most of the Company&#146;s employees at its facility in San Diego, California in the first half of 2009.&#160; Assembled workforce amortization was recorded in research and development expense. The Company recorded assembled workforce amortization of zero, $28,000 and $0.2 million in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Deferred Rent and Other Noncurrent Liabilities</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred rent and other noncurrent liabilities represents deferred rent expense on our facilities in Tarrytown, NY and San Diego, CA.&#160; In accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S., the Company recognizes rental expense, including tenant improvement allowances, on a straight-line basis over the life of the leases or useful life, whichever is shorter, irrespective of the timing of payments to or from the lessor.&#160; The Company ceased use of its discovery research facility in San Diego, CA as a result of the Company&#146;s decision to discontinue its drug discovery activities in 2009.&#160; In accordance with ASC 420-10, &#147;Exit or Disposal Cost Activities&#148; (&#147;ASC 420-10&#148;), the Company recorded a liability of $0.8 million, included in research and development expense on the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss, on the cease-use date based on the fair value of the costs that are expected to be incurred under the lease of the facility.&#160; The fair value of the liability at the cease-use date&nbsp;was determined based on the remaining rental payments, reduced by estimated sublease rental income that could be reasonably obtained for the property. The Company had deferred rent of $0.4 million and $0.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively, that is being amortized through October&nbsp;2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company performs impairment tests on its long-lived assets when circumstances indicate that their carrying amounts may not be recoverable. If required, recoverability is tested by comparing the estimated future undiscounted cash flows of the asset or asset group to its carrying value. If the carrying value is not recoverable, the asset or asset group is written down to fair value. No such impairments have been identified with respect to the Company&#146;s long-lived assets, which consist primarily of property and equipment at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Derivatives</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for its derivative instruments in accordance with ASC 815-10, &#147;Derivatives and Hedging&#148; (&#147;ASC 815-10&#148;).&#160; ASC 815-10 establishes accounting and reporting standards requiring that derivative instruments, including derivative instruments embedded in other contracts, be recorded on the balance sheet as either an asset or liability measured at its fair value. ASC 815-10 also requires that changes in the fair value of derivative instruments be recognized currently in results of operations unless specific hedge accounting criteria are met. The Company has not entered into hedging activities to date. As a result of certain financings, derivative instruments were created that were measured at fair value and marked to market at each reporting period. Changes in the derivative value were recorded as change in value of warrants and derivatives on the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;text-indent:.1pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s only element of accumulated other comprehensive loss was foreign currency translation adjustments of ($1.0) million and ($1.3) million at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company applies ASC 820, <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures </i>(&#147;ASC 820&#148;) to all financial instruments that are being measured and reported on a fair value basis, non-financial assets and liabilities measured and reported at fair value on a non-recurring basis, and disclosures of fair value of certain financial assets and liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following fair value hierarchy is used in selecting inputs for those instruments measured at fair value that distinguishes between assumptions based on market data (observable inputs) and the Company&#146;s assumptions (unobservable inputs).&#160; The hierarchy consists of three levels:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 1 &#151; Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 2 &#151; Inputs other than Level 1 that are observable for similar assets or liabilities either directly or indirectly.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level 3 &#151; Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The financial instruments recorded in the Company&#146;s Consolidated Balance Sheets consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents, accounts payable and the Company&#146;s debt obligations.&#160; The carrying amounts of the Company&#146;s cash and cash equivalents and accounts payable approximate fair value due to their short-term nature.&#160; The fair market value of the Company&#146;s convertible and non-convertible loans is based on the present value of their cash flows discounted at a rate that approximates current market returns for issues of similar risk.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amount and estimated fair values of the Company&#146;s debt instruments are as follows:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:8.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fair</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;font-weight:bold;"><br>    </font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;Value</font></b></p>    </td>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-05, &#147;Comprehensive Income (Topic 220) &#151; Presentation of Comprehensive Income&#148; which amends ASC 220, &#147;Comprehensive Income&#148;.&#160; ASU 2011-05 gives an entity the option to present the total comprehensive income, the components of net income, and the components of other comprehensive income either in a single continuous statement of comprehensive income or in two separate but consecutive statements. ASU 2011-05 is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2011.&#160; The Company adopted the provisions of ASU 2011-05 on a retrospective basis in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. The adoption of ASU 2011-05 did not have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2011, the FASB issued ASU 2011-04, &#147;Amendments to Achieve Common Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure Requirements in GAAP and IFRS&#148;, which amends ASC 820<i>  </i>&#147;Fair Value Measurement&#148;.&#160; ASU 2011-04 improves the comparability of fair value measurements presented and disclosed in financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards. The amended guidance changes the wording used to describe many requirements in U.S. GAAP for measuring fair value and for disclosing information about fair value measurements. Additionally, the amendments clarify the FASB&#146;s intent about the application of existing fair value measurement and disclosure requirements.&#160; ASU 2011-04 is effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2011.&#160; The Company adopted the provisions of ASU 2011-04 beginning on January&nbsp;1, 2012. The adoption of ASU 2011-04 did not have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;7, 2009, the FASB issued ASU 2009-13, &#147;Multiple Revenue Arrangements - a Consensus of the FASB Emerging Issues Task Force&#148; which supersedes certain guidance in ASC 605-25, &#147;Revenue Recognition-Multiple Element Arrangements,&#148; and requires an entity to allocate arrangement consideration to all of its deliverables at the inception of an arrangement based on their relative selling prices (i.e., the relative-selling-price method). The use of the residual method of allocation will no longer be permitted in circumstances in which an entity recognized revenue for an arrangement with multiple deliverables subject to ASC 605-25. ASU 2009-13 also requires additional disclosures. The Company adopted the provisions of ASU 2009-13 beginning on January&nbsp;1, 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">3. License Agreements</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Meda AB</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2010, the Company entered into an exclusive commercialization agreement for Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;with Meda AB (&#147;Meda&#148;), a leading international specialty pharmaceutical company based in Stockholm, Sweden.&#160; Under the terms of the agreement, the Company granted Meda the right to market Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;in Europe and several other countries including Japan, China, and Australia.&#160; The Company received a $3.0 million fee on signing and an additional $2.0 million milestone payment in May&nbsp;2010 upon the first commercial sale of Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;in a major European market, which have been deferred and are being recognized as revenue ratably over the life of the commercialization agreement with Meda.&#160; Additional potential payments include a $5 million payment upon achievement of a regulatory milestone and up to $30 million in sales-based milestones that commence upon attainment of at least $50 million in annual sales. The Company will also receive an escalating percentage royalty on net sales in the covered territories ranging from the low teens to the low twenties and is responsible for Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#146;s commercial supply.&#160; The initial term of this agreement is ten years and is subject to automatic two year extensions at Meda&#146;s option. The agreement can be terminated at any time by Meda upon six months prior written notice.&#160; The agreement can also be terminated by mutual agreement or for cause.&#160; The Company recognized revenue from Meda relating to the signing fee and milestone payment of approximately $0.5 million and $0.4 million in 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160; The Company recognized revenue relating to commercial sales of Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;of approximately $39,000 and $0.2 million in 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160; No revenue was recognized from Meda prior to January&nbsp;2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 6.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Hellstrand</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 6.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company entered into a royalty agreement with Dr.&nbsp;Kristoffer Hellstrand in October&nbsp;1999, under which the Company has an exclusive license to certain patents for Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;configured for the systemic treatment of cancer, infectious diseases, autoimmune diseases and other medical conditions. A predecessor company previously paid Dr.&nbsp;Hellstrand $1 million and agreed to pay a royalty of 1% on net sales of Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; The Company expanded its collaboration with Dr.&nbsp;Hellstrand in November&nbsp;2009 by concluding a new agreement in which the Company acquired rights to develop certain new compounds.&#160; As compensation for this agreement and for providing certain ongoing consulting services, the Company awarded Dr.&nbsp;Hellstrand options to purchase 50,000 shares of its common stock having a fair value of $0.1 million and agreed to pay a monthly consulting fee.&#160; This agreement was terminated in 2011.&#160; The Company paid $0.1 million in 2010 and an inconsequential amount in 2011 in royalties to Dr.&nbsp;Hellstrand.&#160; No royalties were paid to Dr.&nbsp;Hellstrand prior to 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Epitome/Dalhousie</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company entered into a direct license with Dalhousie University in July&nbsp;2007, under which the Company was granted an exclusive license to certain patents for the topical use of tricyclic anti-depressants and NMDA antagonists as topical analgesics for neuralgia that were licensed to Epitome by Dalhousie University. These, and other patents, cover the combination treatment consisting of amitriptyline and ketamine in AmiKet</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. This technology has been incorporated into AmiKet</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has been granted worldwide rights to make, use, develop, sell and market products utilizing the licensed technology in connection with passive dermal applications. The Company is obligated to make payments to Dalhousie upon achievement of specified milestones and to pay royalties based on annual net sales derived from the products incorporating the licensed technology. The Company is obligated to pay Dalhousie an annual maintenance fee until the license agreement expires or is terminated, or an NDA for AmiKet</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;is filed with the FDA, or Dalhousie will have the option to terminate the contract. The license agreement with Dalhousie terminates upon the expiration of the last to expire licensed patent.&#160; The Company paid Dalhousie a maintenance fee of $0.5 million in each of the years 2011, 2010 and 2009.&#160; These payments were expensed to research and development in their respective years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Myrexis,&nbsp;Inc.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with its merger with Maxim Pharmaceuticals on January&nbsp;4, 2006, EpiCept acquired a license agreement with Myrexis Inc. (&#147;Myrexis&#148;) under which the Company licensed the MX90745 series of caspase-inducer anti-cancer compounds to Myrexis. Under the terms of the agreement, Maxim granted to Myrexis a research license to develop and commercialize any drug candidates from the series of compounds during the Research Term (as defined in the agreement) with a non-exclusive, worldwide,</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-15<a name="PB_15_010658_7056"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">royalty-free license, without the right to sublicense the technology. Myrexis is responsible for the worldwide development and commercialization of any drug candidates from the series of compounds. Maxim also granted to Myrexis a worldwide royalty bearing development and commercialization license with the right to sublicense the technology. The agreement requires that Myrexis make licensing, research and milestone payments to the Company totaling up to $27 million, of which $3.0 million was paid and recognized as revenue by Maxim prior to the merger on January&nbsp;4, 2006, assuming the successful commercialization of the compound for the treatment of cancer, as well as pay an escalating mid to high single digit percentage royalty on product sales.&#160; The Company received a milestone payment of $1.0 million in March&nbsp;2008, following dosing of the first patient in a Phase II registration sized clinical trial, which has been deferred and is being recognized as revenue ratably over the life of the last to expire patent that expires in July&nbsp;2024.&#160; Myrexis announced in February&nbsp;2012 that it has suspended company-wide operations pending the outcome of an evaluation of available strategic alternatives to enhance shareholder value that is being undertaken by the investment bank Stifel Nicolaus Weisel on behalf of Myrexis&#146; Board of Directors.&#160; Myrexis is initiating an alignment of resources consistent with its decision to suspend further development activities. The Company is closely monitoring the developments and intends to enforce its rights as appropriate under its license agreement with Myrexis.&#160; The Company recorded revenue from Myrexis of approximately $0.1 million in each of the years 2011, 2010 and 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">DURECT Corporation</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company entered into a license agreement with DURECT Corporation (&#147;DURECT&#148;) in December&nbsp;2006, pursuant to which it granted DURECT the exclusive worldwide rights to certain of its intellectual property for a transdermal patch containing bupivacaine for the treatment of back pain. Under the terms of the agreement, EpiCept received a $1.0 million payment which has been deferred and is being recognized as revenue ratably over the life of the last to expire patent that expires in March&nbsp;2020. The Company amended its license agreement with DURECT in September&nbsp;2008.&#160; Under the terms of the amended agreement, the Company granted DURECT royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual and irrevocable rights to the intellectual property licensed as part of the original agreement in exchange for a cash payment of $2.25 million from DURECT, which has also been deferred and is being recognized as revenue ratably over the last patent life.&#160; The Company recorded revenue from DURECT of approximately $0.3 million in each of the years 2011, 2010 and 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Endo Pharmaceuticals Inc.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company entered into a license agreement with Endo Pharmaceuticals Inc. (&#147;Endo&#148;) in December&nbsp;2003, under which it granted Endo (and its affiliates) the exclusive (including as to the Company and its affiliates) worldwide right to commercialize LidoPAIN BP. The Company also granted Endo worldwide rights to use certain of its patents for the development of certain other non-sterile, topical lidocaine containing patches, including Lidoderm</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, Endo&#146;s topical lidocaine-containing patch for the treatment of chronic lower back pain. Upon the execution of the Endo agreement, the Company received a non-refundable payment of $7.5 million, which has been deferred and is being recognized as revenue on the proportional performance method. The Company is eligible to receive payments of up to $52.5 million upon the achievement of various milestones relating to product development and regulatory approval for both the Company&#146;s LidoPAIN BP product and licensed Endo products, including Lidoderm</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, so long as, in the case of Endo&#146;s product candidate, the Company&#146;s patents provide protection thereof. The Company is also entitled to receive royalties from Endo based on the net sales of LidoPAIN BP. These royalties are payable until generic equivalents to the LidoPAIN BP product are available or until expiration of the patents covering LidoPAIN BP, whichever is sooner. The Company is also eligible to receive milestone payments from Endo of up to approximately $30.0 million upon the achievement of specified net sales milestones for licensed Endo products, including Lidoderm</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, so long as the Company&#146;s patents provide protection thereof. The future amount of milestone payments the Company is eligible to receive under the Endo agreement is $82.5 million. The Company recorded revenue from Endo of approximately $27,000, $14,000 and $24,000 in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the license agreement, the Company is responsible for continuing and completing the development of LidoPAIN BP, including the conduct of all clinical trials and the supply of the clinical products necessary for those trials and the preparation and submission of the NDA in order to obtain regulatory approval for LidoPAIN BP. Endo remains responsible for continuing and completing the development of Lidoderm</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;for the treatment of chronic lower back pain, including the conduct of all clinical trials and the supply of the clinical products necessary for those trials.&#160; No progress in the development of LidoPAIN BP or Lidoderm with respect to back pain has been reported. Accordingly, the Company does not expect to receive any further cash compensation pursuant to this license agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has the option to negotiate a co-promotion arrangement with Endo for LidoPAIN BP or similar product in any country in which an NDA (or foreign equivalent) filing has been made within thirty days of such filing. The Company also has the right to terminate its license to Endo with respect to any territory in which Endo has failed to commercialize LidoPAIN BP within</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-16<a name="PB_16_010724_5335"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Shire BioChem</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maxim entered into a license agreement reacquiring the rights to the MX2105 series of apoptosis inducer anti-cancer compounds from Shire Biochem,&nbsp;Inc (formerly known as BioChem Pharma,&nbsp;Inc.) in March&nbsp;2004 and as amended in January&nbsp;2005, which had previously announced that oncology would no longer be a therapeutic focus of the company&#146;s research and development efforts. Under the agreement, all rights and obligations of the parties under the July&nbsp;2000 agreement were terminated and Shire BioChem agreed to assign and/or license to the Company rights it owned under or shared under the prior research program. The agreement did not require any up-front payments, however, the Company is required to provide Shire Biochem a portion of any sublicensing payments the Company receives if the Company relicenses the series of compounds or make milestone payments to Shire BioChem totaling up to $26.0 million, assuming the successful commercialization of the compounds by the Company for the treatment of a cancer indication, as well as pay a royalty on product sales. The Company accrued a license fee expense of $0.5 million upon the commencement of a Phase I clinical trial for crolibulin</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;in 2006.&#160; This amount, and approximately $0.2 million in interest, remains accrued and unpaid at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">EpiCept GmbH, a wholly-owned subsidiary of EpiCept, entered into a ten-year non-amortizing loan in the amount of &#128;1.5 million with Technologie-Beteiligungs Gesellschaft mbH der Deutschen Ausgleichsbank (&#147;tbg&#148;) in August&nbsp;1997. The loan initially bore interest at 6% per annum.&#160; The loan was amended several times resulting in extensions of the repayment period and an increase in the interest rate to 7.38%.&#160; The loan was repaid in full in June&nbsp;2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)&nbsp; The Company issued $25.0&nbsp;million in principal aggregate amount of 7.5556% convertible subordinated notes due February&nbsp;2014 and five and-a-half year warrants to purchase approximately 4.2&nbsp;million shares of common stock at an exercise price of $3.105 per share in February&nbsp;2009.&#160; Each $1,000 in principal aggregate amount of the notes was initially convertible into approximately 371 shares of Common Stock, at the option of the holders or upon specified events, including a change of control, and if the Company&#146;s common stock trades at or greater than $5.10 a share for 20 out of 30&nbsp;days, beginning February&nbsp;9, 2010. Upon any conversion or redemption of the notes, the holders would receive a make-whole payment in an amount equal to the interest payable through the scheduled maturity of the converted or redeemed notes, less any interest paid before such conversion or redemption. Interest was due and payable on the notes semi-annually in arrears on June&nbsp;30 and December&nbsp;31, beginning on June&nbsp;30, 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company allocated the $25.0 million in proceeds between the convertible subordinated notes and the warrants based on their relative fair values. The Company calculated the fair value of the warrants at the date of the transaction at approximately $8.8 million with a corresponding amount recorded as a debt discount. The debt discount is being accreted over the life of the outstanding convertible subordinated notes using the effective interest method. At the date of the transaction, the fair value of the warrants of $8.8 million was determined utilizing the Black-Scholes option pricing model under the following assumptions: dividend yield of 0%, risk free interest rate of 1.99%, volatility of 118% and an expected life of five years.&#160; The Company recognized approximately $8.6 million of non-cash interest expense in 2009 related to the accelerated accretion of the debt discount as a result of the conversion of $24.5 million of the convertible subordinated notes into approximately 9.1 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remaining $0.5 million of convertible subordinated notes plus approximately $0.1 million in make-whole interest was repaid in June&nbsp;2011, prior to the note&#146;s scheduled maturity.&#160; The Company recognized approximately $0.1 million of non-cash interest expense in 2011 related to the accelerated accretion of the remaining debt discount.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company entered into a six-year non-interest bearing promissory note in the amount of $0.8 million with Pharmaceutical Research Associates,&nbsp;Inc., (&#147;PRA&#148;) in July&nbsp;2006&#160; as compensation for PRA assuming liability on a lease of premises in San Diego, CA. The fair value of the note (assuming an imputed 11.6% interest rate) was $0.6 million and broker fees amounted to $0.2 million at issuance. The note is payable in seventy-two equal installments of $11,000 per month. The loan balance at December&nbsp;31, 2011 was $0.1 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company entered into a senior secured term loan in the amount of $8.6 million with Midcap Financial, LLC., (&#147;Midcap&#148;) in May&nbsp;2011.&#160; The Company had the option to borrow an additional $2.0 million from Midcap on or before December&nbsp;31, 2011 upon meeting certain conditions, including the commencement of a Phase III clinical trial, which it did not exercise. The interest rate on the loan is 11.5% per year. The Company incurred approximately $0.1 million in issuance costs in connection with the loan and is required to pay a $0.3 million fee on the maturity date of the loan.&#160; In addition, the Company issued five year common stock</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">purchase warrants to Midcap granting them the right to purchase 1.1 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $0.63 per share. The basic terms of the loan require monthly payments of interest only through November&nbsp;1, 2011, with 30 monthly payments of principal and interest that commenced on December&nbsp;1, 2011. Any outstanding balance of the loan and accrued interest is to be repaid on May&nbsp;27, 2014. In connection with the terms of the loan agreement, the Company granted Midcap a security interest in substantially all of the Company&#146;s personal property including its intellectual property.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company allocated the $8.6 million in proceeds between the term loan and the warrants based on their relative fair values. The Company calculated the fair value of the warrants at the date of the transaction at approximately $0.5 million with a corresponding amount recorded as a debt discount. The debt discount is being accreted over the life of the outstanding term loan using the effective interest method. At the date of the transaction, the fair value of the warrants of $0.5 million was determined utilizing the Black-Scholes option pricing model utilizing the following assumptions: dividend yield of 0%, risk free interest rate of 1.71%, volatility of 110% and an expected life of five years.&#160; The Company recognized approximately $0.2 million of non-cash interest expense in 2011 related to the accretion of the debt discount.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s term loan with Midcap contains a subjective acceleration clause, which allows the lender to accelerate the loan&#146;s due date in the event of a material adverse change in the Company&#146;s ability to pay its obligations when due.&#160; The Company believes that its losses from operations, its stockholders&#146; deficit and a cash balance that is lower than its loan payable increase the likelihood of the due date being accelerated in this manner, and therefore the Company has classified loan repayments due more than twelve months from the date of these financial statements as a short term liability. The original deferred financing fees and debt discount continue to be amortized over the life of the debt that was assumed when the obligation was originally recorded.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 18.2pt;text-indent:-18.2pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">7. Preferred Stock</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has authorized 5 million undesignated preferred shares as of December&nbsp;31, 2011.&#160; No such preferred stock was issued and outstanding as of December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.&#160; The Company issued preferred shares subsequent to December&nbsp;31, 2011 as described in Note 14.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">8. Common Stock and Common Stock Warrants</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon receipt of the approval of stockholders in July&nbsp;2009, the Company amended its certificate of incorporation to increase the number of authorized shares of common stock from 175,000,000 to 225,000,000 shares.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:14.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company issued five-year common stock purchase warrants in the May&nbsp;2011 Midcap financing, granting Midcap the right to purchase 1.1 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $0.63 per share. The warrants issued to Midcap met the requirements of and are being accounted for as equity in accordance with ASC 815-40. The fair value of the warrants was $0.5 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company raised $4.6 million in gross proceeds, $4.3 million net of $0.3 million in transaction costs, in March&nbsp;2011 through a public offering of common stock and common stock purchase warrants registered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 registering the issuance and sale of up to $50.0 million of the Company&#146;s common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, convertible debt securities and/or warrants to purchase the Company&#146;s securities.&#160; Approximately 7.1 million&nbsp;shares of the Company&#146;s common stock were sold at a price of $0.65 per share.&#160; Five year common stock purchase warrants were issued to investors and the placement agent granting them the right to purchase approximately 5.3 million and 0.4 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $0.72 and $0.8125 per share, respectively.&#160; The Company allocated the $4.6 million in gross proceeds between the common stock and the warrants based on their relative fair values.&#160; Approximately $1.7 million of this amount was allocated to the warrants. The warrants meet the requirements of and are being accounted for as equity in accordance with ASC 815-40.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company raised $7.1 million in gross proceeds, $6.6 million net of $0.5 million in transaction costs, in February&nbsp;2011 through a public offering of common stock and common stock purchase warrants registered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 registering the issuance and sale of up to $50.0 million of the Company&#146;s common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, convertible debt securities and/or warrants to purchase the Company&#146;s securities.&#160; Approximately 8.9 million&nbsp;shares of the Company&#146;s common stock were sold at a price of $0.80 per share.&#160; Five year common stock purchase warrants were issued to investors and the placement agent granting them the right to purchase approximately 3.6 million and 0.4 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $0.75 and $1.00 per share, respectively.&#160; The Company allocated the $7.1 million in gross proceeds between the common stock and the warrants based on their relative fair values.&#160; Approximately $1.7 million of this amount was allocated to the warrants. The warrants meet the requirements of and are being accounted for as equity in accordance with ASC 815-40.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company raised $2.0 million in gross proceeds, $1.9 million net of $0.1 million in transactions costs, in November&nbsp;2010 through a public offering of common stock and common stock purchase warrants registered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 registering the issuance and sale of up to $50.0 million of the Company&#146;s common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, convertible debt securities and/or warrants to purchase the Company&#146;s securities.&#160; Approximately 3.3 million&nbsp;shares of the Company&#146;s common stock were sold at a price of $0.61 per share.&#160; Five year common stock purchase warrants were issued to investors granting them the right to purchase approximately 1.3 million and 0.2 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $0.56 and $0.7625 per share, respectively.&#160; The Company allocated the $2.0 million in gross proceeds between the common stock and the warrants based on their relative fair values.&#160; Approximately $0.5 million of this amount was allocated to the warrants. The warrants meet the requirements of and are being accounted for as equity in accordance with ASC 815-40.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company raised $6.7 million in gross proceeds, $6.2 million net of $0.5 million in transactions costs, in June&nbsp;2010 through a public offering of common stock and common stock purchase warrants registered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 registering the issuance and sale of up to $50.0 million of the Company&#146;s common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, convertible debt securities and/or warrants to purchase the Company&#146;s securities.&#160; Approximately 6.1 million&nbsp;shares of the Company&#146;s common stock were sold at a price of $1.10 per share.&#160; Five year common stock purchase warrants were issued to investors granting them the right to purchase approximately 4.6 million and 0.3 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $1.64 and $1.375 per share, respectively.&#160; In addition, one year common stock purchase warrants were issued to investors granting them the right to purchase approximately 6.1 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $1.64 per share.&#160; The Company allocated the $6.7 million in gross proceeds between the common stock and the warrants based on their relative fair values.&#160; Approximately $3.2 million of this amount was allocated to the warrants. The warrants meet the requirements of and are being accounted for as equity in accordance with ASC 815-40.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company raised $9.6 million in gross proceeds, $8.9 million net of $0.7 million in transaction costs, in June&nbsp;2009 through a public offering of common stock and common stock purchase warrants registered pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form&nbsp;S-3 registering the issuance and sale of up to $50.0 million of the Company&#146;s common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, convertible debt securities and/or warrants to purchase the Company&#146;s securities.&#160; Approximately 4.0 million&nbsp;shares of the Company&#146;s common stock were sold at a price of $2.40 per share.&#160; Two and one-half year common stock purchase warrants were issued to investors granting them the right to purchase approximately 1.4 million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at an exercise price of $2.70 per share.&#160; The Company allocated the $9.6 million in gross proceeds between the common stock and the warrants based on their relative fair values.&#160; Approximately $2.0 million of this amount was allocated to the warrants. The warrants did not meet the requirements of being accounted for as equity in accordance with ASC 815-40 since the Company did not have an adequate number of authorized shares to reserve for the exercise of the warrants. Therefore, the value of the warrant shares were classified as a liability and were marked to market at June&nbsp;30, 2009 resulting in a loss of $0.3 million in the statement of operations and comprehensive loss.&#160; The warrants were reclassified from liability to equity in accordance with ASC 815-40 as a result of stockholders approving an increase in the number of authorized shares of the Company&#146;s common stock in July&nbsp;2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">9. Commitments and Contingencies</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Leases</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases facilities and certain equipment under agreements through 2014 accounted for as operating leases. The leases generally contain renewal options and require the Company to pay all executory costs such as maintenance and insurance. The Company renewed its lease in Munich, Germany in January&nbsp;2011, through July&nbsp;2014.&#160; Rent expense approximated $1.1 million, $1.1 million and $1.3 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, 2010, and 2009, respectively.</font></p>

<td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.52%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Consulting Contracts and Employment Agreements</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a party to a number of research, consulting, and license agreements, which require the Company to make payments to the other party upon the other party attaining certain milestones as defined in the agreements.&#160; The Company may be required to make future milestone payments as of December&nbsp;31, 2011, totaling approximately $5.4 million, under these agreements, of which approximately $3.0 million is payable during 2012 and approximately $2.4 million is payable from 2013 through 2015. The Company is obligated to make future royalty payments to three of its collaborators under existing license agreements, including one based on net sales of Ceplene</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">one based on net sales of AmiKet</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;and one based on net sales of crolibulin</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TM</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">, to the extent revenues on such products are realized. Under the Company&#146;s agreement with Dalhousie University, the Company is obligated to pay an annual maintenance fee so long as no commercial product sales have occurred and the Company desires to maintain its rights under the license agreement.&#160; The Company paid Dalhousie a maintenance fee of $0.5 million in each of the years 2011, 2010 and 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Board of Directors ratified the employment agreements between the Company and its chief executive officer and chief financial officer dated as of October&nbsp;28, 2004. The employment agreements covered the term through December&nbsp;31, 2010, and provide for base salary, discretionary compensation, stock option awards, and reimbursement of reasonable expenses in connection with services performed under the employment agreements. The agreements also compensate such officers in the event of their death or disability, termination without cause, or termination within one year of an initial public offering or a change of control, as defined in the respective employment agreements.&#160; Both employment agreements were automatically renewed for another year, ending December&nbsp;31, 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Litigation</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;25, 2008 plaintiffs Kenton L. Crowley and John A. Flores filed a complaint against EpiCept in the United States District Court, New Jersey, which was transferred on March&nbsp;20, 2009 to the United States District Court for the Southern District of California.&#160; The complaint alleges breach of contract, breach of covenant of good faith and fair dealing, fraud, and rescission of contract with respect to the development of a topical cream containing ketamine and butamben, known as EpiCept NP-2.&#160; Discovery was conducted in 2010 and 2011 and is now complete.&#160; The Company filed a motion for summary judgment on April&nbsp;29, 2011, which was granted in the Company&#146;s favor on January&nbsp;24, 2012.&#160; Therefore, in 2011 the Company reversed the reserve of approximately $0.2 million that was previously recorded.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">10. Share-Based Payments</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company records stock-based compensation expense at fair value in accordance with ASC 718-10, &#147;Compensation &#151; Stock Compensation&#148; (&#147;ASC 718-10&#148;).&#160; The Company utilizes the Black-Scholes valuation method for determination of share-based compensation expense. Certain assumptions need to be made with respect to utilizing the Black-Scholes valuation model, including the expected life, volatility, risk-free interest rate and anticipated forfeiture of the stock options.&#160; The expected life of the stock options was calculated using the method allowed by the provisions of ASC 718-10.&#160; In accordance with ASC 718-10, the simplified method for &#147;plain vanilla&#148; options may be used where the expected term is equal to the vesting term plus the original contract term divided by two. The risk-free interest rate is based on the rates paid on securities issued by the U.S. Treasury with a term approximating the expected life of the options. Estimates of pre-vesting option forfeitures are based on the Company&#146;s experience. The Company will adjust its estimate of forfeitures over the requisite service period based on the extent to which actual forfeitures differ, or are expected to differ, from such estimates. Changes in estimated forfeitures will be recognized through a cumulative catch-up adjustment in the period of change and will also impact the amount of compensation expense to be recognized in future periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for stock-based transactions with non-employees in which services are received in exchange for the equity instruments based upon the fair value of the equity instruments issued, in accordance with ASC 718-10 and ASC 505-50, &#147;Equity-</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-21<a name="PB_21_011355_5335"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Based Payments to Non-Employees.&#148; The two factors that most affect charges or credits to operations related to stock-based compensation are the estimated fair market value of the common stock underlying stock options for which stock-based compensation is recorded and the estimated volatility of such fair market value. The value of such options is periodically remeasured and income or expense is recognized during the vesting terms.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">2005 Equity Incentive Plan</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2005 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#147;2005 Plan&#148;) was adopted on September&nbsp;1, 2005, approved by stockholders on September&nbsp;5, 2005 and became effective on January&nbsp;4, 2006. The 2005 Plan provides for the grant of incentive stock options, within the meaning of Section&nbsp;422 of the Internal Revenue Code, to EpiCept&#146;s employees and its parent and subsidiary corporations&#146; employees, and for the grant of nonstatutory stock options, restricted stock, restricted stock units, performance-based awards and cash awards to its employees, directors and consultants and its parent and subsidiary corporations&#146; employees and consultants. Options are granted and vest as determined by the Board of Directors. A total of 13,000,000 shares of EpiCept&#146;s common stock are reserved for issuance pursuant to the 2005 Plan.&#160; No optionee may be granted an option to purchase more than 1,500,000 shares in any fiscal year. Options issued pursuant to the 2005 Plan have a maximum maturity of 10 years and generally vest over 4 years from the date of grant.&#160; The Company records stock-based compensation expense at fair value.&#160; The Company issued approximately 1.4 million options to purchase common stock at a weighted average exercise price of $0.86 per share to certain of its employees and members of its board of directors and 0.3 million restricted stock units to members of its board of directors in 2011.&#160; The Company estimates that $0.8 million of stock based compensation related to 2011 options and restricted stock units granted will be recognized as compensation expense over the vesting period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.2in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected life of the stock options was calculated using the method allowed by the provisions of ASC 718-10.&#160; In accordance with ASC 718-10, the simplified method for &#147;plain vanilla&#148; options may be used where the expected term is equal to the vesting term plus the original contract term divided by two. The Company used its historical volatility rate in 2011, 2010 and 2009, as management believes that this rate will be representative of future volatility over the expected term of the options.&#160; The risk-free interest rate is based on the rates paid on securities issued by the U.S. Treasury with a term approximating the expected life of the options. The Company has never paid cash dividends, and does not currently intend to pay cash dividends, and thus has assumed a 0% dividend yield.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Pre-vesting forfeitures. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimates of pre-vesting option forfeitures are based on the Company&#146;s experience. Currently, the Company uses a forfeiture rate of 10%. The Company will adjust its estimate of forfeitures over the requisite service period based on the extent to which actual forfeitures differ, or are expected to differ, from such estimates. Changes in estimated forfeitures will be recognized through a cumulative catch-up adjustment in the period of change and will also impact the amount of compensation expense to be recognized in future periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Following the departure of a former director in 2011, the Company agreed to extend the period during which he would be entitled to exercise certain vested stock options to purchase the Company&#146;s common stock from three months following the effective date of his resignation, June&nbsp;14, 2011, to the expiration date of each option granted to the former director.&#160; Additionally, all options that were not vested on the date of his resignation will continue to vest.&#160; The Company recorded compensation expense related to the modification of the exercise period and vesting period of $32,000 in the second quarter of 2011.&#160; Additional compensation expense of $30,000 will be recognized over the remaining vesting period of one year for the non-vested options.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Following the departure of a former director in 2009, the Company agreed to extend the period during which he would be entitled to exercise certain vested stock options to purchase the Company&#146;s common stock from three months following the effective date of his resignation, February&nbsp;3, 2009, to six months following such effective date. The Company recorded compensation expense related to the modification of the exercise period of $3,000 in the first quarter of 2009.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The total remaining unrecognized compensation cost related to non-vested stock options, restricted stock and restricted stock units amounted to $1.1 million at December&nbsp;31, 2011, which will be amortized over the weighted-average remaining requisite service period of 2.2 years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 15.85pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Stock</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted stock was issued to certain employees in 2007, and entitled the holder to receive a specified number of shares of the Company&#146;s common stock over a four year, monthly vesting term.&#160; This restricted stock grant is accounted for at fair value at the date of grant and an expense was recognized during the vesting term. All restricted stock grants vested in 2010.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 15.85pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Stock Units</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restricted stock units were issued to certain employees and non-employee members of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors in 2011, 2009 and 2008, which entitle the holder to receive a specified number of shares of the Company&#146;s common stock at the end of the one year, two year or four year vesting term.&#160; This restricted stock unit grant is accounted for at fair value at the date of grant and an expense is recognized during the vesting term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">2009 Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 7.9pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2009 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &#147;2009 ESPP&#148;) was adopted by the Board of Directors on December&nbsp;19, 2008, subject to stockholder approval, and was approved by the stockholders at the Company&#146;s 2009 Annual Meeting held on June&nbsp;2, 2009. The 2009 ESPP was effective on January&nbsp;1, 2009 and a total of 1,000,000 shares of common stock have been reserved for sale. The 2009 ESPP is implemented by offerings of rights to all eligible employees from time to time. Unless otherwise determined by the Company&#146;s Board of Directors, common stock is purchased for accounts of employees participating in the 2009 ESPP at a price per share equal to the lower of (i)&nbsp;85% of the fair market value of a share of the Company&#146;s common stock on the first day the offering or (ii)&nbsp;85% of the fair market value of a share of the Company&#146;s common stock on the last trading day of the purchase period. The initial period commenced January&nbsp;1, 2009 and ended on June&nbsp;30, 2009.&#160; Each subsequent offering period will have a six-month duration.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The number of shares to be purchased at each balance sheet date is estimated based on the current amount of employee withholdings and the remaining purchase dates within the offering period.&#160; The fair value of share options expected to vest is estimated using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.&#160; Share options for employees entering the 2009 ESPP were estimated using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model and the assumptions noted on the table below.</font></p>
