<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">11. Income Taxes</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred income taxes reflect the net effects of temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities for financial reporting purposes and the amounts used for income tax purposes. The Company&#146;s deferred tax assets relate primarily to its net operating loss carryforwards and other balance sheet basis differences. In accordance with ASC 740, &#147;Income Taxes,&#148; the Company recorded a valuation allowance to fully offset the net deferred tax asset, because it is not more likely than not that the Company will realize future benefits associated with these deferred tax assets at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010. The change in the valuation allowance for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010 was an increase of approximately $5.8 million and $11.9 million, respectively. The increases in the valuation allowance of $11.9 million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2010 were net of an increase in the valuation allowance of $6.2 million as a result of adjustments to the gross deferred tax asset related to the net operating loss carryforward due to an adjustment to the ownership change under Internal Revenue Code Section&nbsp;382 in 2009, which was subsequently adjusted in 2010. Significant components of the Company&#146;s deferred tax assets at December&nbsp;31, 2011 and 2010 are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The principal differences between the U.S. statutory tax rate of 34% and the Company&#146;s effective tax rates of (0)% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, 2010 and 2009 is primarily due to the Company&#146;s valuation allowance and the write-down of net operating loss carryforwards due to an ownership change under Internal Revenue Code Section&nbsp;382 in 2009.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:13.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has approximately $280.3&nbsp;million of net operating loss carryforwards (federal, state and foreign) and tax credit carryforwards of $3.7&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2011. The Company reduced its tax attributes (NOL&#146;s and tax credits) as a result of the Company&#146;s ownership changes in 2009 and 2007 and the limitation placed on the utilization of its tax attributes as a substantial portion of the NOL&#146;s and tax credits generated prior to the ownership change will likely expire unused. Accordingly, the federal NOL&#146;s were reduced by approximately $272.0&nbsp;million and the tax credit carryforwards were reduced by approximately $7.3&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">14. Subsequent Events (Unaudited)</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company filed a Certificate of Designation in Delaware on February&nbsp;8, 2012, which designated 2,000 shares of its authorized preferred shares as Series&nbsp;A 0% Convertible Preferred Stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company received $1.8 million cash, net of $0.2 million in transaction costs, in February&nbsp;2012 from the issuance of 2,000 shares of the Company&#146;s Series&nbsp;A 0% Convertible Preferred Stock, at a price of $1,000 per share, and warrants to purchase 5.0 million shares of the Company&#146;s Common Stock.&#160; The Shares of Preferred Stock were convertible into an aggregate of 10.0 million shares of the Company&#146;s Common Stock.&#160; A total of 1,224 shares of Preferred Stock were converted into approximately 6.1 million shares of the Company&#146;s Common Stock as of March&nbsp;23, 2012.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:15.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company reduced the exercise price and extended the expiration date of the Company&#146;s outstanding Series&nbsp;B Common Stock Purchase Warrants that were issued in a registered direct offering that closed on June&nbsp;30, 2010 (the &#147;Series&nbsp;B Warrants&#148;) effective January&nbsp;9, 2012. The Series&nbsp;B Warrants, which originally would have expired at the close of business on January&nbsp;9, 2012, are exercisable for up to 6,136,363 shares of the Company&#146;s common stock; the original exercise price was $1.64 per share. The exercise price has been reduced to $0.20 per share, and the expiration date has been extended to the close of business on the earlier of (i)&nbsp;April&nbsp;9, 2012 or (ii)&nbsp;a date selected by the Company in its sole discretion, with respect to which date the Company provides written notice to the warrant holder not less than ten business days in advance.&#160; A total of 3.8 million warrants were exercised for proceeds of $0.8 million as of March&nbsp;23, 2012.</font></p>
